name: Pediatric retrograde ESIN entry approaches to the femur
corridor: Paired medial and lateral distal-metaphyseal windows at the same level, 2–3 cm proximal to the distal femoral growth plate and centered sagittally

positioning.text: Position supine with the knee and distal femur accessible and the full femur imageable on orthogonal views.

setup.text: Map the distal femoral physis, template two equal elastic nails and balanced curves, and ensure reduction and imaging from knee to hip.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial and lateral epicondyles, joint line, distal femoral physis under fluoroscopy, shaft center, and symmetric planned entry levels.

incision.text: Make separate approximately 3-cm medial and lateral incisions beginning at each entry and extending distally to permit oblique nail advancement.

superficial_interval.text: Spread fascia and muscle bluntly on each side to expose cortex while protecting medial neurovascular and lateral soft-tissue structures.

deep_interval.text: Create entries at the same axial level, 2–3 cm proximal to the growth plate, centered in the shaft on the sagittal plane and directed away from the physis.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, medial or lateral fascia and muscle, periosteum, distal metaphyseal cortex, then medullary canal.

structures_encountered.text: Distal femoral physis, medial and lateral metaphyseal cortex, vastus medialis and lateralis, periosteum, and canal are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: The distal femoral physis, saphenous nerve and vein medially, lateral soft tissues, cortex, knee capsule, and femoral vessels with uncontrolled medial passage are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Entry closer than 2 cm to the physis risks growth injury; asymmetric, posterior, or closely placed portals risk cortical split, malalignment, or soft-tissue injury.

retraction_hazards.text: Use blunt dissection and protective sleeves to bone; avoid blind medial clamping, forceful nail-end levering, and soft-tissue entrapment around rotating nails.

exposure.text: Provides balanced paired retrograde access to the femoral canal while avoiding the hip and leaving the fracture zone closed.

limitations.text: Best suited to appropriately sized children and length-stable diaphyseal patterns; heavier children and unstable proximal or distal patterns have less reliable control.

extensions.text: Lengthen either incision for controlled cortical visualization rather than accepting an uncertain percutaneous portal or prominent nail end.

indications.text: Use for selected pediatric femoral-shaft fractures in children whose size, fracture stability, and canal can support balanced elastic fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Favor another construct for length-unstable patterns, very proximal or distal fractures, inadequate canal size, severe obesity, local infection, or inability to protect the physis.

implant_implications.text: Use two equal-diameter precontoured nails with opposing bends and symmetric entries; bury or trim ends to avoid knee and soft-tissue irritation without preventing removal.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm physeal distance and sagittal centering for both portals, then monitor canal passage, reduction, length, axes, rotation, and final nail-end position.

closure.text: Confirm hemostasis and nonprominent nail ends, release entrapped soft tissue, and close subcutaneous tissue and skin, preferably with absorbable sutures.

complications.text: Complications include physeal injury, cortical split, malalignment or shortening, nail migration, medial or lateral irritation, knee stiffness, infection, delayed union, and refracture.

bailouts.text: If a portal is unsafe or the fracture remains unstable after balanced nails, stop, revise the entry or reduction under direct vision, supplement fixation, or change constructs.

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric femoral-shaft fracture is suitable for paired retrograde elastic nails and safe distal metaphyseal entry above the open physis

questions.question: How far proximal to the physis are retrograde ESIN entries?
Where are the entries on the sagittal plane?
questions.answer: In the middle of the femoral shaft.

questions.question: Why are the two portals placed at the same level?
questions.answer: To create balanced opposing elastic fixation and avoid asymmetric deforming forces.
